title: Rollout messaging & fallback states: clarity, edge-case copy, and decision log
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Polish and finalize UX copy, visual treatments, and interaction patterns for rollout states and fallback behaviors in the Console rollout timeline and per-route rollout UI. This ticket covers: (1) microcopy for transient states (queued, throttled, degraded), (2) fallback messaging when model variants are used, (3) compact mobile/compact-tablet phrasing, and (4) final redlines for engineering handoff. Goal: reduce user confusion during degraded capacity/fallbacks and make remediation steps discoverable.
acceptance_criteria: All rollout state variants have approved copy for desktop and mobile (queued, throttled, degraded, fallback-to-variant, rollback-in-progress, canary-success, canary-failure)
Figma file contains redlines and tokens for color/contrast, animation duration, and iconography for each state
Engineering-facing spec doc with example API payloads for rendering messaging (links included) is linked in the ticket
UX QA checklist completed and signed off by PM and Eng lead
Automated visual snapshot tests have reference images and a follow-up ENG task is created for integration
decisions: Use 'Fallback: alternative model used' phrasing instead of 'Degraded - model variant' to keep language product-facing rather than infra-facing
Include a persistent 'Why did this happen?' affordance on throttled/degraded states that opens the rollout history panel
Use amber (#D98A00) for transient warning states and red (#D04444) only for actionable failures (rollback or canary-failure)
Prefer concise mobile copy limited to 40 characters where possible; expanded copy appears in tooltip or expanded detail pane
tradeoffs: Longer explanatory copy reduces repeated support questions but increases UI density; mitigated by layering copy (short + expand)
Using different color semantics for transient vs permanent failures adds cognitive overhead for new users but improves signal for experienced operators
Embedding remediation links increases discoverability but creates coupling with documentation URLs that can change; we reference doc IDs rather than absolute links in copy where possible
